Create a summarise AST node

Source: R/ast.R
ast_summarise.Rd

Create a summarise AST node

Usage

ast_summarise(
  input,
  aggregations,
  groups,
  result_groups = character(),
  on_sum_overflow = "error",
  group_order = "keys"
)

Arguments

input

Input AST node

aggregations

List of aggregation structures

groups

Character vector of group columns this node aggregates BY (drives the actual groupby op – always the full pre-summarise group set, regardless of .groups=)

result_groups

Character vector of group columns RETAINED on the summarise's output: a subset of groups, computed from .groups= semantics by resolve_summarise_groups() (R/summarise.R) – character() for .groups = "drop"/ungrouped input, all of groups for "keep", all-but-the-last for the default/ "drop_last". Read by propagate_groups() (R/execute.R).

on_sum_overflow

What to do when an integer/logical sum() leaves R's integer range at execution. "double": the column comes back FLOAT64, as in dplyr (eager mode reconciles the schema from the result). "error" (lazy plans, whose schema was declared INT32 statically): raise cuplyr_error_sum_overflow. A lazy summarise() plans only a sum of a logical this way: an INT32 sum runs at the verb with "double".

group_order

Row order of a grouped result: "keys" sorts by the group keys (ascending, NA last), dplyr's group_by() order; "first" (#50) orders groups by first appearance, dplyr's .by = order, and is what summarise_by_desugar() asks for.

Value

An ast_summarise node
